Reggression test first (failed on unfixed, passes after): test_a_refuted_triage_answers_a_reworded_copy_under_a_different_digest. Fix: _sibling_copy matches a sibling's same-design-point copy under a different digest, recording the verdict on that copy's own digest.

chunk_findings.detail: When multiple findings in the sibling gate share the same design point (for example, two different findings reported on the same file/symbol location, but with different digests), `_sibling_copy` iterates over the list of findings and picks the first one whose digest is different from the input digest and whose verdict is unsettled. If the first finding matching the design point happens to be a completely different, unrelated finding that just happens to be on the same file/symbol and has not been triaged yet, `_sibling_copy` will incorrectly select it as the "reworded copy" of the triaged finding, applying the triage verdict to the wrong finding under the sibling gate.

evidence.note: Bug Bc771f31635: ddflow cadence --ran NOPE as a --repro-cmd appended cadence.ran/ddflow.seen to the real committed .ddflow/events. Root cause: reprocheck ran in a LINKED worktree (git worktree add), whose .git pointer resolves the primary, so a ddflow child writes the shared log.

Live-lease check: reprocheck.py was free (added to globs); reprobundle.py already mine. Tests cannot write the shared log: regression asserts no cadence.ran NOPE event lands in primary .ddflow/events.

Regression test first (failed: cadence.ran NOPE appeared in real log; passes after): tests/test_repro_cmd_isolated.py. Fix: _isolated_clone makes a full standalone clone at the recorded sha (not git worktree add); _prime_scratch resets the clone per run. 35 repro tests pass.

chunk_findings.detail: The switch to a full clone drops the old “never follow a poisoned `.git`” guard, and the new comment is false. `_prime_scratch` runs `git clean` / `git reset --hard` in the clone with no check that `scratch/.git` is a real directory. A multi-run repro (`[bugs] repro_runs` > 1) whose command is `url=$(git config --get remote.origin.url); rm -rf .git && ln -s "$url/.git" .git` (origin is the operator repo, set by `git clone --local`) leaves a symlink. The next prime follows it, so `git reset --hard <sha>` moves the real repository’s HEAD and index. The filing is supposed to never change the project; this path does.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/reprocheck.py:_prime_scratch

chunk_findings.detail: A multi-run repro can point the clone's `.git` at the operator repo before the next prime, and `_prime_scratch` then runs `git clean` / `git reset --hard` with no check that `.git` is still this clone's directory. The deleted worktree path refused a symlink and restored a pristine gitdir pointer before any git command for exactly this reason; the new comment that a corrupted `.git` "never" writes the operator tree is false. Given `repro_runs >= 2` and a command `real=$(git config --get remote.origin.url); rm -rf .git; ln -s "$real/.git" .git` (origin is the real repo path `git clone --local` records), the second `_prime_scratch` resolves GIT_DIR to the operator's `.git` and `reset --hard <sha>` moves that repo's HEAD and index.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/reprocheck.py:_prime_scratch

data.probe: fixed: _prime_scratch now refuses a .git that is not a real directory BEFORE any git command (gitdir.is_symlink() or not is_dir() -> False, run unreached), and _isolated_clone removes the origin remote after checkout, so no path back to the operator repo is discoverable. Regression test test_a_poisoned_dot_git_is_refused_not_followed fails on the unfixed path and passes after.
data.title: ddflow/services/reprocheck.py:_prime_scratch

data.probe: fixed: _prime_scratch now refuses a .git that is not a real directory BEFORE any git command, and the clone's origin remote is removed after checkout; regression test refuses the symlinked .git and fails on unfixed. Re-run reviewer needed on the current tree.
data.title: ddflow/services/reprocheck.py:_prime_scratch

chunk_findings.detail: The new `.git` directory/symlink check does not stop a multi-run repro from steering the framework’s own git commands onto the operator tree. With `[bugs] repro_runs` > 1 and a command that only edits the clone (`git config core.worktree /path/to/the/operator/repo`), `.git` is still a real directory, so the check returns and the next iteration’s `git clean -xdfq -f` and `git reset --hard sha` honor `core.worktree` and clean/reset the real checkout. That command does not itself touch the project; `_prime_scratch` does, which is the same class of write-back this guard claims to close.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/reprocheck.py:_prime_scratch

chunk_findings.detail: `origin` is not the remote clone always creates, and the remove result is ignored. `git clone` names the remote from `clone.defaultRemoteName` (global/system config, default `origin`). Given `clone.defaultRemoteName=upstream`, `G.run(dst, "remote", "remove", "origin")` fails, checkout still proceeds, and `git remote get-url upstream` is the absolute path of the operator repo. A repro such as `url=$(git remote get-url upstream); …` can append to the real `.ddflow/events` on the first run, which is the bug this clone is supposed to fix.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/reprocheck.py:_isolated_clone

chunk_findings.detail: The symlink refusal does not stop a multi-run repro from steering the next prime onto the operator tree. `.git` only has to stay a real directory: with `repro_runs >= 2`, the first command `git config core.worktree <operator-checkout>` writes that into the clone's own config; the next `_prime_scratch` sees `is_symlink()` false and `is_dir()` true, then runs `git clean -xdfq -f` and `git reset --hard`, which honor `core.worktree` and clean/reset the real checkout. That is the same class of mutation bug Bc771f31635 was filed for, and removing `origin` does not affect it.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/reprocheck.py:_prime_scratch

chunk_findings.detail: `G.run(dst, "remote", "remove", "origin")` still assumes the remote is named `origin` and ignores the result. `git clone` names the remote from `clone.defaultRemoteName` (default `origin`). With `clone.defaultRemoteName=upstream`, that remove fails, checkout still proceeds, and `git remote get-url upstream` is the absolute path of the operator repo. A first-run repro such as `url=$(git remote get-url upstream); …` can append into the real `.ddflow/events`. The fresh-clone change does not close this; the help text that the origin remote is removed is false for that config.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/reprocheck.py:164

chunk_findings.detail: The second regression never exercises the isolation it claims. `evil` only runs `git config core.worktree <operator>` and exits; there is no second git command, no second `bug_found`/`repro_runs` pass, and the assertion only compares `HEAD`. On unfixed code that still executes the repro in the operator checkout, that `git config` rewrites the operator `.git/config` and leaves `HEAD` unchanged, so the test passes. The same vacuous check also passes if a later run honors a planted `core.worktree` or a non-`origin` remote and appends into `.ddflow/events`, because those writes do not move `HEAD`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_repro_cmd_isolated.py:71

chunk_findings.detail: The per-run checkout path is the predictable `tails / f"run-{nth}"`, and `_one_run` is invoked with that directory as cwd, so a repro line can pre-create the next destination with a relative path the old code deliberately hid. Given `[bugs] repro_runs` ≥ 2 and `--repro-cmd 'mkdir ../run-1'` (or `ln -s <real-repo> ../run-1`), run 0 succeeds and run 1 starts against an attacker-made path. The deleted comment recorded that a poisoned run must not be able to mkdir the next run's path because that name was never on argv; `run-0`, `run-1`, … puts it back. If `_isolated_clone` refuses an existing dest, later runs are counted `unreached` and a reproducing command is reported `executed: False` / unavailable instead of failed; if it writes into or follows that path, isolation is gone and the next clone can land on the operator tree.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/reprocheck.py:_isolated_clone call

chunk_findings.detail: `test_a_poisoned_clone_config_cannot_steer_a_later_run_onto_the_operator_repo` does not lock the failure it names. The repro only runs `git config core.worktree <operator>` (which does not move HEAD) and then `exit 1`; there is no second repro run and no later git write (commit, checkout, or `cadence`) through that config. Given an unfixed runner that reuses one clone and honors `core.worktree`, `rev-parse HEAD` is still `head0`, so the test passes while a follow-up write in the same clone would land in the operator tree.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_repro_cmd_isolated.py:51

chunk_findings.detail: The `proj` fixture accepts `repo` and `monkeypatch`, but `conftest.py` in this test suite does not define a `repo` fixture (the project convention or standard pytest fixtures use `tmp_path` or `git_repo`). Running pytest on `tests/test_repro_cmd_isolated.py` crashes immediately with `fixture 'repo' not found` for every test in the file, preventing the test suite from executing.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_repro_cmd_isolated.py:27

chunk_findings.detail: The earlier objection still holds. The docstring and name require a later repro run to honor a planted `core.worktree` and then fail to write the operator repo, but `test_a_poisoned_clone_config_cannot_steer_a_later_run_onto_the_operator_repo` still calls `K.bug_found` only once. The added `git commit --allow-empty` runs in that same process, so a reused clone whose config was poisoned by run 1 is never started. Given a second `repro_runs` that keeps the clone and honors `core.worktree=<operator>`, this test still passes: `HEAD` and `log --all` are only checked after the single filing, and "steal" never has to appear in a follow-up run.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_repro_cmd_isolated.py:50
